correctness.rationale: Backward Euler is a scaled orthogonal map, with squared gain f(t)=1/(1+2at+r²t²). Independently, the slope magnitude of the chord from (0,1) is (1−f(t))/t=(2a+r²t)/(1+2at+r²t²); the derivative has the sign of r²−(2a+r²t)². For r>2a its unique peak at s=(r−2a)/r² gives a global supporting line touching only at 0 and s, and f is strictly convex from s onward by the displayed second derivative. At an interior mean of the affine face, equality in the line bound fixes the two masses. For h>s the tangent of the convex minorant has a unique contact at h on the whole half-line; at h=s the first supporting line restricts the support to {0,s} and the mean forces the point mass. For r≤2a strict convexity holds even at the r=2a boundary (f''>0 for t>0). The lower bounds apply to arbitrary finite-mean laws by the affine supporting-line inequalities. Replacing the zero atom by ε and reweighting gives the positive-only nonattainment result; i.i.d. stages multiply the expected gains. The rational example and positive approximants were independently spot-checked.
residual_risks: Line 61's zero set {0,s} is understood after restriction to [0,s]; globally f equals its minorant on all of [s,∞). No change to the equality argument.
The frozen finite-support trials are supplementary, not an all-law check. The result is for a fixed mean per attempted stage, not deterministic elapsed time.

value.rationale: A complete boundary classification for a standard integrator answers when variance can actually improve a natural mean-square damping metric and whether any strictly positive law attains it. The exact split is more useful than a local failure of Jensen: it specifies the optimizer for every mean and reveals the skipped-stage obstruction. Its value is as a benchmark, not as a speed or accuracy claim.
residual_risks: Restricted to planar normal modes and a per-attempt expectation; no fixed-time accuracy, cost reduction, or advantage for adaptive schemes follows.
